title: Use a short recursive query
summary: A recursive CTE can use earlier results to make later ones.
introduction: A recursive CTE can use earlier results to make later ones. Your task: Change the stop value to 5.
learningObjectives: Explain the example for use a short recursive query

blocks.text: A recursive CTE can use earlier results to make later ones. It needs a stopping rule so it does not repeat forever.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.code: WITH RECURSIVE numbers(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM numbers WHERE n<4) SELECT n FROM numbers;
blocks.title: Use a short recursive query

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `WITH RECURSIVE` repeats a query from an initial result. Its stopping rule must prevent endless growth.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Always understand the stop condition. Recursion limits are a guard, not a replacement for a correct rule.
